summary.text: 后 is an old graph used for a ruler and, in received texts, a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes the separate word “after,” represented by 後 in traditional Chinese; this spelling use is attributed to the words’ reported sound similarity, though an ancient sound match is not established here.

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. An early lexicographic account reads it as a human figure issuing commands and analyzes it through 一 and 口. Other accounts connect early forms with 司 or 毓. None settles the graphic origin of the received form, which cannot be securely decomposed as a picture of childbirth or a body part.

components.text: 口 is visible in the received graph and appears in the early lexicographic analysis. Its independent meaning or pictorial role in the graph’s origin is not established.

history.text: Accounts of the early graph differ: one identifies 后 and 司 as the same graph, with orientation distinctions in bronze forms; another reports an oracle form written with 毓. Neither account provides a settled sequence leading to the received form.
The received graph includes 口, but the available early lexicographic analysis does not establish how this visible form arose. No component-by-component graphic sequence is settled.

uncertainties.text: The early graphic origin of 后 remains disputed. Childbirth and rear-body interpretations are reported, but decisive paleographic evidence for either depiction or a secure decomposition is not provided.

The classical use of 后 for 後 and the precise history of their modern consolidation are reported through a search-result record whose target page could not be inspected; their chronology remains unresolved.

senses.period: Late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions (reported; primary examples not independently verified)
senses.text: A late Spring and Autumn bronze use is reported with the sense “ruler”; any earlier oracle use of the same graph and word is not securely dated here.

senses.period: Received textual usage; transition date unresolved
senses.text: Received-text examples document 后 for a ruler’s principal wife. They do not date a development from “ruler” to this sense.

senses.period: Classical spelling use reported; precise chronology unresolved; current in simplified Chinese
senses.text: In simplified Chinese, 后 writes the separate word “after/behind,” for which traditional Chinese uses 後. This is a spelling borrowed for that word, not a meaning shown to have developed from “ruler.” Both graphs have modern Mandarin reading hòu, but an ancient sound match is not established here.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but the evidence does not show when or how one developed from the other.

The graph 后 was reused to write the distinct word represented by 後 because the words were reported to sound alike or similarly. Both are pronounced hòu in modern Mandarin; an ancient sound match and the loan’s precise chronology are not established here.

limitations.text: The available attestations do not establish a dated semantic chain from childbirth, succession, or “ruler” to “empress.”

overview.text: 后 has been used for a ruler and a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes “after”: the separate graph 後 was borrowed for this word because the words were reported to sound alike, though an ancient sound match is not established here.

components.text: 口 appears in the received graph and in an early analysis, but its original role in 后 is unsettled.
